question: What is the main purpose of body cavities in human anatomy?

options.A: To produce hormones for metabolic balance
options.B: To digest nutrients absorbed from food
options.C: To pump blood throughout the body systems
options.D: To protect and support internal organs

explanation: Body cavities act as safe, enclosed spaces that cushion internal organs against physical trauma. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h1)

question: What are the two main cavities that divide the inside of the human body?
explanation: You've got this! The human body splits its main internal spaces into the dorsal cavity at the back and the ventral cavity at the front. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following structures is found inside the cranial cavity?
explanation: The cranial cavity is formed by the skull bones and specifically houses the brain. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient with a back injury to the vertebrae has damage in which body cavity?
explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cavity is enclosed by the backbone (vertebral column) and holds the delicate spinal cord. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which muscular structure separates the chest (thoracic) cavity from the belly (abdominopelvic) cavity?
explanation: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped breathing muscle that forms a neat floor for the chest and a roof for the belly. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the name of the specific space that directly surrounds and protects the human heart?
explanation: Think 'peri' for around and 'cardio' for heart! The pericardial cavity is the cozy, fluid-filled space right around your heart. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which of these organs is found in the upper belly (abdominal) part of the abdominopelvic cavity?
explanation: Your stomach hangs out in the upper tummy area, while your bladder is tucked way down in the pelvis. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do nurses divide the belly into four quarters (quadrants) during physical checks?

options.A: To measure lung capacity during deep breathing exercises
options.B: To accurately locate and document patient pain or organ issues
options.C: To determine the exact heart rate of the patient
options.D: To physically separate the stomach from the urinary bladder

explanation: Dividing the tummy into quadrants helps nurses easily pinpoint and write down exactly where a patient is feeling pain. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is there fluid between the thin membranes that wrap around our organs?

options.A: To transmit nerve signals to the brain
options.B: To digest food particles in the stomach
options.C: To carry oxygen through the bloodstream
options.D: To reduce friction during organ movement

explanation: Imagine two sliding doors with oil between them. This fluid lubricates the membranes so your heart and lungs can glide smoothly without rubbing raw! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h5)

question: What do we call the layer of a membrane that is stuck directly onto the surface of an organ?
explanation: Remember: 'visceral' relates to the internal organs themselves, while 'parietal' lines the outer wall of the cavity. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h5)

question: A patient complains of sharp pain in their lower right tummy. Which organ should a nurse suspect right away?
explanation: Classic clinical scenario! The appendix is typically tucked away in the lower right quarter of the abdomen. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h6)

question: A patient has fluid building up around their lungs in the pleural cavity. What main problem will this cause?

options.B: Blockage of food in the esophagus
options.C: Complete failure of the urinary bladder

explanation: Extra fluid takes up space, squeezing the lungs and making it hard for them to puff out fully when breathing in. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h6)
